rust/src/tests/accounting_integration.rs: A shared counter records the engine's backing-file operations.
Format and open a volume through the public accounting interface. Write a block, read it and close the volume.
The bytes must match. Writes for data and the final checkpoint must all be charged, with no uncompleted reservations or errors.
The formatter starts with a backing file and a ledger that counts physical writes and syncs.
Create an empty volume, then inspect the ledger rather than estimating work from file size.
The table and two checkpoint descriptors cost three 4096-byte writes and two syncs. Nothing should remain pending.
A formatted volume has an independent counter for physical reads, writes and syncs.
Take counter readings before and after a write, read back the block, then close the volume.
The data must match. Closing should add three metadata writes and two syncs; bytes reserved must equal bytes completed.
An empty checkpoint describes ranges of logical blocks that have no data on disk.
Load its index while counting actual reads of the backing file.
The loader should find empty mappings with only three block reads. It must not read nonexistent pages, write data or sync the file.
The engine has an older usable checkpoint and a changed mapping page in memory.
Try to save a replacement checkpoint with different limits on how many bytes may be written.
If the budget runs out, the old checkpoint stays current and the changed page remains unsaved. With enough space the new checkpoint becomes current.
The mapping cache is full and has one changed page. The backing-write budget covers only part of a checkpoint.
Read another logical block so the engine must save that page before it can make room.
Return no-space without changing the read buffer. Count the completed page write, not a successful checkpoint. Refuse subsequent flush and close.
Opening the volume uses the entire test allowance for backing writes.
Try to write block zero, then try to read it and flush.
Reject the write for lack of space before recording any new mapping or live bytes. Further operations must fail; the failed read must leave its buffer untouched.
Block zero already contains a saved value. After startup the remaining write budget covers one block, less than the proposed record.
Attempt to overwrite block zero and compare the planned destination before and after.
Return no-space, mark the allowance exhausted and leave the destination unchanged. Reopening must still return the earlier value.
The backing-operation counter can classify only supported request types.
Submit a request with an operation code it does not recognize.
Reject the request as invalid input. Count one error, leave no request pending and mark the completion totals incomplete rather than presenting them as reliable.
A volume contains one saved client block and is open with I/O accounting.
Shorten the backing file so the engine cannot read a full block from the saved address.
Report a short read, not a completed block read. Count the error, mark the totals incomplete and refuse clean close.
rust/src/tests/allocations.rs::detects_a: Other tests rely on a counter to detect unexpected heap allocation.
Measure code that allocates, then measure a calculation that simply returns 42.
The counter must detect at least one allocation in the first case and none in the second. This checks the measuring tool, not disk behavior.
rust/src/tests/checkpoint_batches.rs::ch: A checkpoint must save changed mapping pages in batches, including when a page count falls just above a batch boundary.
Close volumes with 1, 2, 31, 32, 33 and 65 changed pages. Inspect the stored records and I/O counts.
All pages must be accounted for in order, with correct links and a newer usable checkpoint.
rust/src/tests/checkpoint_batches.rs::sh: Saving a checkpoint would free cache space for another read. There are 65 changed mapping pages.
Make a checkpoint write stop partway through a batch. Try further requests and inspect the backing file after restart.
Stop the volume without publishing the incomplete checkpoint. Recover across a whole-block cut; reject recognizable damaged metadata without changing the file.
rust/src/tests/checkpoint_batches.rs::mi: The engine writes a batch of 65 mapping snapshots to a temporary volume.
Replace one snapshot with zeros, leaving later records intact. Repeat with the gap at different positions, then reopen.
The later records cannot complete a checkpoint across the gap. Recovery must still return the expected client data.
rust/src/tests/checkpoint_batches.rs::ba: Closing a volume writes its changed mapping pages before it publishes a new checkpoint.
Kill the child process at selected page, descriptor and sync boundaries during close. Open the same file in the surviving process.
The engine must recover the data for all 65 changed pages, even when the child never finishes close.
rust/src/tests/checkpoint_replay.rs::cle: The client writes two blocks, then overwrites block zero before closing the volume.
Inspect the saved map, read the physical blocks it identifies and check their recorded checksums.
The map must refer to the newer value for block zero and the original value for block one. Count two live blocks, not three writes.
rust/src/tests/checkpoint_replay.rs::pay: The client flushes two known blocks. One copy has a close-time checkpoint; another must recover from the log.
Damage the stored bytes for just one block, leaving its recorded checksum and the other block intact.
Reject a read of the damaged version without touching the caller's buffer. Reads of unaffected data and a subsequent valid replacement must succeed.
rust/src/tests/checkpoint_replay.rs::fal: Two checkpoints provide alternative starting points for recovery. Valid records follow the older one.
Damage the descriptor that identifies the newer checkpoint, then reopen the volume.
Start from the older usable checkpoint and apply the valid later records. The client must still read the expected values, not just the older checkpoint's state.
The newest checkpoint points to a page that identifies saved mappings. An older checkpoint is still available.
Damage the newer checkpoint's index page without damaging the older one or the later valid log records.
Reopen from the older checkpoint and recover the later updates. Falling back must not discard those client writes.
rust/src/tests/checkpoint_replay.rs::rej: A disk image has two possible starting points for recovery.
Corrupt the newer checkpoint descriptor and a page needed by the older checkpoint. Attempt to open the volume twice.
Both attempts must return an invalid-data error, without a panic or any change to the damaged image.
rust/src/tests/checkpoint_replay.rs::rec: An engine checkpoint contains two saved writes. The test then constructs valid later records directly in its backing file.
Reopen the image and inspect the reconstructed write position, mappings, checksums and live space.
The engine should resume after the last valid record, with four live blocks and the expected data at each address.
rust/src/tests/checkpoint_replay.rs::rej: The engine accepts an option that limits how much log data it must replay at startup.
Try invalid values on an existing file and a missing path. Compare the existing file with its original contents.
Reject the invalid option before modifying or creating a file. A valid configuration should still open normally.
rust/src/tests/checkpoint_replay.rs::che: The engine holds writes in memory and has a limit on how much log history may accumulate after a checkpoint.
Send groups of buffered writes until the next group would exceed that limit, then reopen.
Save a checkpoint before exceeding the limit. Later records may follow the checkpoint; recovering them must return the latest complete values.
rust/src/tests/checkpoint_replay.rs::log: A small volume already stores a live block and cannot reclaim enough space for an overwrite.
Try another value for the same address while the existing data is still needed.
Return no-space without relocating live data or changing the mapping. The old value must remain readable rather than disappearing with the rejected write.
rust/src/tests/checkpoint_replay.rs::flu: A newly formatted volume has an initial checkpoint and one new client write.
Flush the write without asking the engine to close and save a new checkpoint. Open the backing file again.
The checkpoint sequence should still identify the original checkpoint, but recovery should return the flushed bytes.
rust/src/tests/checkpoint_replay.rs::clo: Two client blocks have new mappings that are not part of the original empty checkpoint.
Close the volume, inspect the new checkpoint descriptor and follow its pointers to the saved mappings. Then reopen.
The alternate descriptor should identify the new checkpoint. Its mappings and checksums, and those loaded after restart, must agree.
An open volume has no mapping changes that need a new checkpoint.
Close it and compare checkpoint state before and after close, including a repeat without further updates.
Closing must not publish a different checkpoint simply because the caller closed the volume.
rust/src/tests/checkpoint_replay.rs::equ: Two checkpoint slots claim the same position in the log.
First place equivalent checkpoint descriptions in both slots. Then change a table pointer in one and recompute its checksum so it still looks intact.
Accept the matching descriptions. Reject the conflicting pair as invalid rather than choosing a version arbitrarily.
rust/src/tests/cleaner_thread.rs::delaye: A background worker reads blocks so the engine can reclaim partially unused disk regions.
Delay that worker's reads. Ask for maintenance several times before the worker signals that it has finished.
Those calls should report waiting promptly without issuing foreground reads. The completion signal must wake the engine so it can copy the two live blocks and preserve their data.
rust/src/tests/cleaner_thread.rs::pressu: Writes have used the immediately available space, but a background worker can still find space to reclaim.
Delay the worker's report while the client keeps writing.
The engine must wait for the report and free space, not tell the client that all space is occupied. The expected block values must remain intact.
rust/src/tests/cleaner_thread.rs::close_: A background worker is updating its view of the volume and reading a range of blocks for reclamation.
Close the volume while that work is still outstanding, then reopen it and read back the blocks.
Close must finish with the worker stopped. All expected values must survive, and the engine's counts of used and free space must balance.
rust/src/tests/cleaner_thread.rs::a_fail: The cleaner is reading data that it may have to copy before the engine frees a disk region.
Inject an error in the cleaner's read, then attempt another write and another maintenance operation.
The engine must report the error and stop accepting both kinds of work. Reopening must still return the expected client data.
rust/src/tests/cleaner_thread.rs::schedu: A client repeatedly overwrites a small set of blocks. A scheduler decides when the engine should reclaim unused storage.
Compare runs with and without scheduled maintenance, including idle intervals and periods of continuous requests.
With scheduling enabled, maintenance must run both when idle and when its deadline arrives. Client writes must keep making progress without a false no-space error.
rust/src/tests/cleaner_thread.rs::idle_m: A client continually replaces data so that old copies occupy space the engine can reclaim.
Allow idle maintenance between writes and then read back the last values.
The engine must actually free regions rather than continually moving the same data. Writes must continue without a false no-space error and return the latest data.
rust/src/tests/cleaner_thread.rs::aged_q: A temporary 256 MiB backing file holds a working set of 16384 logical blocks.
Overwrite blocks chosen by a repeatable generator, with periodic flushes and scheduled maintenance. Flush, close and reopen the aged volume.
The workload must finish; opening the resulting checkpoint, inspecting space use and closing again must succeed. This is not a byte-by-byte readback test.
rust/src/tests/format_geometry.rs::publi: A 673-block volume needs three pages to describe where its data lives.
Open with several cache budgets and read empty blocks while recording cache capacity, hits, misses and memory use.
The engine must report the requested budget separately from effective capacity. Reads should return zeros, with cache counts appropriate to the capacity.
rust/src/tests/format_geometry.rs::xxh3_: The disk format uses a specific checksum to recognize damaged bytes. Old files depend on that calculation remaining stable.
Calculate checksums for empty input, a zero block and a seeded input containing encoded addresses and data.
Each value must exactly match its fixed reference value; changing the calculation would change the persistent format.
rust/src/tests/format_geometry.rs::forma: The formatter calculates how many logical blocks and physical regions fit in a backing file.
Try valid boundary sizes as well as zero, undersized and oversized layouts and an invalid region size.
Accept the supported layouts and reject the invalid combinations. An invalid request must not create the missing backing file.
rust/src/tests/format_geometry.rs::open_: A freshly formatted image contains two checkpoint descriptors but no client data.
Open it and compare the recovered identity, size, empty mappings and log position with the on-disk descriptors. Exercise mismatched checkpoint descriptions.
The clean image must reconstruct an empty volume at its starting position. Inconsistent descriptions must not silently become a valid volume.
rust/src/tests/format_geometry.rs::forma: The formatter initializes a backing file for an empty volume.
Read both checkpoint descriptors directly, including the version, slot, volume identity, sizes, sequence number and reserved fields.
Each descriptor must contain the expected initial values for its slot. The two records must describe the same empty volume.
Current software expects version four of the disk format.
Give the opener images marked as format three and compare their bytes before and after the attempt.
The engine must reject the older format without changing it. Refusing an unsupported version must not act as an implicit upgrade.
rust/src/tests/format_v4_protocol.rs::fo: An empty format-four volume needs a table of disk regions and two starting records for recovery.
Format a test file, then load its checkpoint and inspect its space map and log position.
Both checkpoint slots must describe the same initial position. The table must occupy its assigned block, the free-region count must agree, and no client block should be live.
rust/src/tests/format_v4_protocol.rs::pu: The engine has changed mappings and must save new snapshots, their index and its space table.
Publish the checkpoint in the alternate slot, try publishing again without changes and inspect both starting points.
The new slot must point to the new metadata; the old slot must remain a usable fallback. The second publish must report no change.
rust/src/tests/format_v4_protocol.rs::re: The engine writes client updates and relocated data to separate regions but numbers the records in a single sequence.
Fill regions, advance to new ones through on-disk links, then reconstruct the volume from the log.
Recovery must follow the links and apply both streams in sequence. The resulting addresses and data must reflect the combined history.
A disk region is reused, leaving an intact record from its earlier use where recovery is looking for a new update.
Present the recovery scanner with the old record, then with damaged or misplaced versions.
It should recognize intact stale data as the end of new updates, but reject the invalid versions. Old bytes must not authorize arbitrary corruption.
rust/src/tests/format_v4_protocol.rs::to: A recovery scan follows data records and metadata that connects one region to the next.
Damage a data record's footer in one image; in other images change the metadata needed to follow the log.
Keep only the complete data prefix before the torn footer. Reject recognizable damaged metadata rather than silently treating it as a safe end.
rust/src/tests/format_v4_protocol.rs::bo: The volume's later writes affect three mapping pages but the recovery cache can hold only one page at a time.
Reopen and replay the records in windows, then inspect the checkpoint and reopen again.
One new checkpoint must describe all five live blocks. No changed page should remain unsaved or be lost when the next window replaces it.
rust/src/tests/format_v4_protocol.rs::li: The engine is about to start writing relocated data into another disk region.
Advance the write position and count the physical operations that record and sync the link. Try advancing again when no free region remains.
The link must be written and synced before use of the new region. A failed advance must not add writes.
rust/src/tests/fsync01.rs::fsync01_contr: Two controls start with flushed old values, then overwrite the same two blocks.
Run once without faults. In the broken control, drop both new records and report a successful flush after repeating only the sync.
The clean copy must contain both new values. The checker must catch both old values in the broken copy; detecting false success is the passing outcome.
rust/src/tests/fsync01.rs::fsync01_engin: The client flushes two old values, then overwrites both blocks with library retry enabled before the writes.
Remove both new records from the backing file at flush and report an I/O error.
The engine must rewrite the saved bytes at their original locations and sync before reporting success. Reopening a copy must return both new values.
rust/src/tests/io_uring.rs::direct_io_ur: The low-level storage path uses the Linux asynchronous I/O interface to write blocks directly to a file.
Write a known block, sync the file, reopen it and read the block back through that interface.
The bytes read after reopen must exactly match the bytes written, not just have the requested length.
rust/src/tests/io_uring.rs::waits_when_s: A Linux asynchronous request can be accepted before any completion is available. An event descriptor lets the test control when a poll completes.
Submit the poll, then make the event readable and wait for completion.
The wait helper must continue after submission and return the matching completion rather than treating an empty completion queue as success.
rust/src/tests/io_uring.rs::destroys_rin: The engine has a Linux asynchronous I/O queue and is waiting for a request to finish.
Make the wait operation report a permanent input/output error.
The caller must receive the original error and the queue must already be destroyed when control returns, so no later work can reuse it.
rust/src/tests/mapping_prefetch.rs::sort: The disk contains 65 adjacent mapping snapshots and the memory cache can hold only four.
Read one logical block from each page in sequence, counting both requested and speculative page reads.
Read-ahead should combine adjacent reads and satisfy 47 later requests from prefetched pages. It must not trigger a checkpoint or discard speculative pages unused.
rust/src/tests/mapping_prefetch.rs::pref: A cache contains a changed mapping page, and some on-disk page locations do not form a consecutive range.
Read successive pages near the changed page, then repeat after closing and reopening the volume.
Read-ahead must not replace the changed mapping, force a checkpoint or fetch across a gap. Reading the changed block must return the client's value.
rust/src/tests/mapping_prefetch.rs::spec: The engine tries to read mapping information ahead of the client's requests. A page in the speculative range contains damaged data.
Read neighboring pages first, then explicitly request the block whose mapping is corrupt.
Do not install the damaged mapping. The direct request must fail, leave the destination buffer untouched and mark the volume failed.
rust/src/tests/mapping_prefetch.rs::shor: A sequential read pattern causes the engine to request several mapping pages together.
Shorten the prefetch read so the engine receives less than the requested amount. Inspect the cache and the caller's buffer.
Fail the read without copying partial data or installing speculative mappings. The volume must also refuse a later flush.
rust/src/tests/mapping_prefetch.rs::nons: A volume has eight mapping pages and a four-page cache.
Read pages in the order 0, 3, 6, 2, 5, 1 instead of reading adjacent pages.
Issue six demand reads and no read-ahead. Missing a page on its own should not cause unrelated pages to be loaded.
rust/src/tests/packed_writes.rs::sorting: An in-memory buffer contains 4096 blocks inserted in reverse address order; one address has already been overwritten.
Sort the buffered addresses, count allocations, check each payload and clear the buffer for reuse.
The addresses must become strictly increasing without allocating more memory. Each address must keep its latest bytes, and the cleared buffer must accept a new write.
rust/src/tests/packed_writes.rs::removin: The write buffer holds entries for several addresses, with distinct payloads to identify each one.
Remove a consecutive range while counting allocations. Look up the removed addresses and their neighbors, then insert a replacement.
Only the requested entries should disappear. The others must retain their bytes; removal must allocate nothing and leave the buffer usable.
rust/src/tests/packed_writes.rs::packed_: The client buffers writes in reverse order, with enough blocks to cross the limit of a single on-disk record.
Flush groups of several sizes and inspect the physical records and backing I/O counts. Reopen the file to read the blocks.
Records must contain the correct sorted addresses, with one log flush for the group. Every address must still have its expected payload.
rust/src/tests/packed_writes.rs::incompa: An engine cannot safely release a buffered group if the mapping cache or checkpoint budget is too small for it.
Attempt to open an image with incompatible settings, then try a supported combination.
Reject the invalid settings without changing any bytes in the file. For valid settings, allocated memory must fit the reported heap budget.
rust/src/tests/packed_writes.rs::pressur: The write buffer holds two blocks and the cache holds two mapping pages.
Repeatedly write addresses on the same two pages; then write a group that needs two different pages. Flush and reopen.
Reusing the same pages needs no pressure checkpoint. The new group should cause one checkpoint, and all four block values must survive.
rust/src/tests/packed_writes.rs::packed_: A single on-disk record can contain updates to several logical blocks.
Kill the engine process at selected points while it is updating the in-memory map for a packed record. Reopen the same backing file.
Recovery must reconstruct all the mappings from the stored record. It must not expose only the entries that reached memory before the process died.
rust/src/tests/packed_writes.rs::preflig: Two writes have already been flushed. A new buffered group needs a checkpoint before the engine can release it.
Kill the child process at different stages of that checkpoint, including writes and syncs of the descriptor, then reopen.
The earlier complete group must still be readable. The not-yet-released group must not appear as a completed update.
